strong.definition: The dimension is applicable, canonically structured, and supported at the reviewed depth and freshness expected for the dimension.

usable.definition: The dimension is applicable and interpretable from canonical structure, but depth, multiplicity, or freshness is below the strong threshold.

partial.definition: The dimension is applicable and has canonical representation, but one or more material fields, relationships, or supporting observations remain incomplete or unresolved.

sparse.definition: The dimension is applicable but canonical representation is minimal, integrity-blocked, or too weak to support normal comparison or dossier use.

absent.definition: The dimension is applicable to the current reviewed scope and no canonical representation is present. This is a knowledge-state statement, not a claim that the real-world feature does not exist.

not_applicable.definition: The dimension is outside the current reviewed planning scope for the asset or is explicitly inapplicable under a source-supported mechanism rule. It is not an unresolved gap.

cross_axis_invariants: Every planning cell must record one planning_state, one applicability_state, and one observation_state.
planning_state not_applicable requires applicability_state not_applicable_to_current_scope and observation_state not_applicable.
planning_state absent requires applicability_state applicable and observation_state unobserved or source_unavailable.
not_applicable never counts as an unresolved gap or queue trigger.
unobserved and source_unavailable are knowledge states and never authorize a negative factual claim.
A source-unavailable state never authorizes fabricated canonical data, an archive URL, or a false boolean.
Historical v1 baselines and queues remain immutable and retain their original semantics.

dimensions.applicability_rule: Every canonical asset requires an identity, naming, lineage, launch-date, and verification boundary.
dimensions.absent_rule: Use absent only if the canonical asset identity or required identity boundary is missing.
dimensions.observation_rule: Identity readiness and canonical asset records provide the observation basis.

dimensions.applicability_rule: Every canonical asset has a lifecycle state and may have material lifecycle history.
dimensions.absent_rule: Use absent when no canonical lifecycle representation exists; do not infer that no lifecycle events occurred.
dimensions.observation_rule: Lifecycle classification and canonical events provide the observation basis.

dimensions.applicability_rule: Every canonical asset requires at least one issuer, protocol, governance, operator, or equivalent organization relationship.
dimensions.absent_rule: Use absent when no canonical relationship row exists.
dimensions.observation_rule: Canonical relationship rows and issuer/protocol boundary readiness provide the observation basis.

dimensions.applicability_rule: Every canonical asset requires a reference, asset-class, backing-model, and stabilization-mechanism interpretation.
dimensions.absent_rule: Use absent only if the mechanism classification itself is missing.
dimensions.observation_rule: Canonical classification and comparison-readiness records provide the observation basis.

dimensions.applicability_rule: Applicable when the canonical mechanism includes reserve, collateral, backing, treasury, or comparable asset-support structure.
dimensions.absent_rule: Use absent only after applicability is established and no canonical reserve/backing representation exists.
dimensions.not_applicable_rule: Use not_applicable only when the reviewed canonical mechanism explicitly excludes reserve or collateral structure and records a reason.
dimensions.observation_rule: Canonical classification, reserve profile, reserve reports, and reserve components provide the observation basis.

dimensions.applicability_rule: Applicable when the issuer or protocol design offers, historically offered, or materially defines a redemption, conversion, burn, or exit mechanism.
dimensions.absent_rule: Use absent only after redemption applicability is established and no canonical redemption profile exists.
dimensions.not_applicable_rule: An explicit source-supported redemption_profile.status of not_applicable maps to planning not_applicable; it must not be converted to partial merely because access or minimum fields are also not_applicable.
dimensions.observation_rule: Canonical redemption profile, comparison readiness, source support, and freshness provide the observation basis.

dimensions.applicability_rule: Every canonical asset has an issuance, minting, creation, or historical issuance mechanism.
dimensions.absent_rule: Use absent when no canonical issuance representation exists.
dimensions.observation_rule: Canonical issuance profile and comparison readiness provide the observation basis.

dimensions.applicability_rule: Every canonical asset has at least one native, issued, or protocol deployment context.
dimensions.absent_rule: Use absent when no canonical deployment row exists.
dimensions.observation_rule: Deployment rows provide the observation basis; unresolved verification fields are maintenance gaps and do not by themselves make an asset a dossier candidate.

dimensions.applicability_rule: Every canonical asset requires a legal-entity, protocol-governance, or explicit decentralized-context profile.
dimensions.absent_rule: Use absent when no canonical legal or governance context exists.
dimensions.not_applicable_rule: Never applicable; decentralized context is represented rather than omitted.
dimensions.observation_rule: Canonical legal profiles, organization relationships, and legal comparison readiness provide the observation basis.

dimensions.applicability_rule: Applicable only when a named jurisdiction, regulator, enforcement event, licensing question, or other bounded regulatory research scope has been reviewed for the asset.
dimensions.absent_rule: Use absent only inside an established regulatory review scope when a required canonical note could not be recorded; absence never means the asset is unregulated or unrestricted.
dimensions.not_applicable_rule: Use not_applicable when no bounded asset-specific regulatory question is part of the current planning scope.
dimensions.observation_rule: Regulatory notes and the named research scope provide the observation basis; generic lack of a note is out of scope, not a dossier defect.

dimensions.applicability_rule: Every canonical asset has a history and may have material canonical events.
dimensions.absent_rule: Use absent when no canonical event row exists; do not infer that no real-world event occurred.
dimensions.observation_rule: Canonical event rows and lifecycle state provide the observation basis.

dimensions.applicability_rule: Every canonical asset requires evidence support for its canonical claims.
dimensions.absent_rule: Use absent when no asset-scoped canonical Evidence identity is linked.
dimensions.observation_rule: Canonical Evidence identities and Evidence Relations provide the observation basis.

dimensions.applicability_rule: Every canonical dossier requires an explicit uncertainty-management boundary, even when no unresolved item has yet been recorded.
dimensions.absent_rule: Use absent when no canonical known-unknown management row exists; this makes no completeness claim.
dimensions.observation_rule: Canonical known-unknown rows provide the observation basis.

dimensions.applicability_rule: Every canonical asset participates in internal comparison-readiness validation.
dimensions.absent_rule: Use absent only if no readiness result can be produced.
dimensions.observation_rule: The Comparison Readiness audit provides the observation basis; this dimension diagnoses structure and does not independently select a dossier batch.

dimensions.applicability_rule: Applicable when at least one included canonical facet has a defined freshness expectation.
dimensions.absent_rule: Use absent only if applicable freshness facets exist but no freshness support can be observed.
dimensions.not_applicable_rule: Use not_applicable when all included facets are explicitly freshness-not-applicable or no included freshness facet exists.
dimensions.observation_rule: Facet Freshness cells provide the observation basis; unsupported anchors are maintenance signals rather than automatic dossier selection.

dimensions.applicability_rule: Applicable only to asset, jurisdiction, platform, function, and effective-date combinations covered by a reviewed Market Access research scope.
dimensions.absent_rule: Use absent only within an established scope when no canonical record could be established; absence never means unavailable, banned, or unsupported.
dimensions.not_applicable_rule: Use not_applicable for assets outside the currently reviewed Market Access scope.
dimensions.observation_rule: Canonical Market Access records plus the named reviewed research scope provide the observation basis.
